The mishna teaches: And when they comfort the king with the meal of comfort, he reclines on the dargash. The Gemara asks: What is a dargash? Ulla says: A bed of fortune, which would be designated in houses for decoration and for good fortune, and no one would sit on it. The Sages said to Ulla: Is there anything which until now we did not authorize one to sit on, but now, in his time of mourning, we seat him on it?

Rava objects to this question: What is the difficulty in this? Perhaps sitting on the dargash is just as it is with eating and drinking. As until now, we did not feed him nor give him drink, but now, in his time of mourning, we feed him and give him drink, in the meal of comfort. Rather, if it is difficult, this is what is difficult, as it is taught in a baraita: Concerning a dargash, the mourner is not required to overturn it during mourning. Rather, he stands it up on its side. And if it enters your mind to say that this is a bed of fortune, why is he not required to overturn it? But isn’t it taught in a baraita: With regard to one who overturns his bed during mourning, not only does he overturns his own bed, but rather he overturns all the beds he has in his house?

The Gemara responds: What is the difficulty in this? Perhaps the lack of requirement to overturn the dargash is just as it is with a bed that is designated for the storage of garments, and not for sleeping, as it is taught in a baraita: If it was designated for the storage of garments and not for people to lie down on, he is not required to overturn it. Rather, if it is difficult, this is what is difficult, as it is taught in a baraita: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: One is not required to overturn a dargash. Rather, the mourner loosens the straps [karvitin] and it falls on its own. And if it enters your mind to say that this is a bed of fortune, does such a bed have straps?

Rather, when Ravin came he said: One of the Sages said to me, and Rav Taḥlifa is his name, that he was often in the market of the leather workers, and he said to him: What is the meaning of dargash? A leather bed. Rabbi Yirmeya says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The difference between a bed and a dargash is this: A dargash

has its weaving on its inside, in that the straps woven to hold the bedding are tied in holes inside the bed posts, while a bed has its weaving on its outside, in that its straps are tied around the posts.

The Gemara raises an objection from the mishna (Kelim 16:1): From when are wooden vessels considered complete and susceptible to impurity? In the case of a bed or a crib, this happens once they are rubbed with fish skin, which smoothens the wood. The Gemara asks: And if a bed is woven on its back side, as Rabbi Yoḥanan claimed, why do I need rubbing with fish skin? Doesn’t the weaving cover the smooth part of the bed? Rather, instead of Rabbi Yoḥanan’s explanation, say that the weaving of both this and that, a dargash and a bed, is on its inside, and the difference between them is that on a bed, the straps go in and out of holes on the posts, whereas on a dargash, they go in and out of loops.

Rabbi Ya’akov says that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi says: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel that a mourner is not required to overturn a dargash, but only to untie the straps around its posts to let it fall on its own. In connection with this matter Rabbi Ya’akov bar Ami says: In the case of a bed whose posts [naklitim] on which the canopy is spread extend, meaning that they are very long, so that the bed will remain high off the ground even if it is overturned, the mourner stands it up in the time of mourning and that is sufficient.

en: GEMARA: The Gemara asks: What is a dargash? Ulla said: It is a bed of good fortune, placed in the house as a fortuitous omen, and not designated for sleeping. The Rabbis said to Ulla: That which we learned in a mishna: When the people serve the king the meal of comfort after he buries a relative, all the people recline on the ground and the king reclines on a dargash during the meal. According to your explanation, during the entire year he does not sit on the bed; on that day of the funeral he sits on it? Ravina objects to the question of the Rabbis: This anomaly is just as it is with regard to meat and wine, as throughout the entire year if he wishes he eats them, and if he wishes he does not eat them; on that day of the funeral, we give him meat and wine in the meal of comfort.

Rather, this is difficult, as it is taught in a baraita with regard to the custom of overturning the beds in the house of a mourner: With regard to a dargash in his house, the mourner would not overturn it, but he merely stands it on its side. And if you say that a dargash is a bed of fortune, isn’t it taught in a baraita: A mourner who is required to overturn his bed is required to overturn not only his own bed, but to overturn all of the beds that he has inside his house, even those not used for sleeping. Why, then, is he not required to overturn the dargash? The Gemara rejects this contention: This is not difficult;

this is just as it is with regard to the case of a bed designated exclusively for vessels, as it is taught in a baraita: If the bed in a mourner’s house was a bed designated for vessels and not for sleeping, one need not overturn it. The same is true with regard to the bed of fortune. Since it is not for sleeping, one need not overturn it.

Rather, if defining a dargash as a bed of fortune is difficult, this is difficult, as it is taught in a baraita that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A mourner need not overturn a dargash; rather, he loosens the loops that connect the straps that support the bedding to the bedframe, and it collapses on its own. And if a dargash is a bed of fortune, does it have loops [karvitin]? When Ravin came from Eretz Yisrael to Babylonia, he said: I asked one of the Sages about the meaning of dargash, and Rav Taḥalifa, from the West, was his name, who frequented the tanners’ market. And he said to me: What is a dargash? It is a leather bed.

It was stated: Which is a bed and which is a dargash? Rabbi Yirmeya said: In a bed, one fastens the supporting straps over the bedframe; in a dargash, one fastens the straps through holes in the bedframe itself. The Gemara raises an objection from a mishna in tractate Kelim (16:1): With regard to wooden vessels, from when are they considered finished vessels and susceptible to ritual impurity? A bed and a crib are susceptible from when he smooths them with the skin of a fish. And the objection is: If in a bed the straps are fastened over the bedframe, why do I need smoothing with the skin of a fish? The wood of the bedframe is obscured from view.

Rather, with regard to both this, a bed, and that, a dargash, one fastens the straps through holes in the bedframes themselves, and the difference between them is: In a bed, the straps are inserted and extracted through holes in the bedframe; in a dargash, the straps are inserted and extracted through loops attached to the bedframe, as Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said that one loosens the loops and the bedding falls on its own.

Rabbi Ya’akov bar Aḥa said that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi said: With regard to a bed whose two posts [nakliteha] protrude, rendering its overturning impossible, he stands it on its side, and that is sufficient for him. Rabbi Ya’akov bar Idi said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel with regard to the overturning of a dargash.
he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי דַּרְגֵּשׁ? אָמַר עוּלָּא: עַרְסָא דְגַדָּא. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְעוּלָּא, הָא דִּתְנַן: כְּשֶׁהֵן מַבְרִין אוֹתוֹ, כׇּל הָעָם מְסוּבִּין עַל הָאָרֶץ וְהוּא מֵיסֵב עַל הַדַּרְגֵּשׁ. כּוּלָּהּ שַׁתָּא לָא יָתֵיב עֲלֵהּ, הָהוּא יוֹמָא יָתֵיב עֲלֵהּ? מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַבָּשָׂר וְיַיִן, דְּכוּלַּהּ שַׁתָּא אִי בָּעֵי — אָכֵיל, וְאִי בָּעֵי — לָא אָכֵיל, הָהוּא יוֹמָא אֲנַן יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ!

אֶלָּא הָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּתַנְיָא: דַּרְגֵּשׁ לֹא הָיָה כּוֹפֵהוּ, אֶלָּא זוֹקְפוֹ. וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ עַרְסָא דְגַדָּא הוּא, וְהָתַנְיָא: הַכּוֹפֶה אֶת מִטָּתוֹ — לֹא מִטָּתוֹ בִּלְבַד הוּא כּוֹפֶה, אֶלָּא כׇּל מִטּוֹת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת הוּא כּוֹפֶה! הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא,
מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַמִּטָּה הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים, דְּתַנְיָא: אִם הָיְתָה מִטָּה הַמְיוּחֶדֶת לְכֵלִים — אֵין צָרִיךְ לִכְפּוֹתָהּ.

אֶלָּא אִי קַשְׁיָא — הָא קַשְׁיָא, דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: דַּרְגֵּשׁ — מַתִּיר קַרְבִּיטָיו וְהוּא נוֹפֵל מֵאֵלָיו. וְאִי דַּרְגֵּשׁ עַרְסָא דְגַדָּא הוּא, קַרְבִּיטִין מִי אִית לֵיהּ? כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר: שְׁאֵילְתֵּיהּ לְהָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן וְרַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא שְׁמֵיהּ, דַּהֲוָה שְׁכִיחַ בְּשׁוּקָא דְצַלָּעֵי, וְאָמַר לִי: מַאי דַּרְגֵּשׁ — עַרְסָא דְצַלָּא.

אִיתְּמַר, אֵיזֶהוּ מִטָּה וְאֵיזֶהוּ דַּרְגֵּשׁ? אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: מִטָּה — מְסָרְגִין אוֹתָהּ עַל גַּבָּהּ, דַּרְגֵּשׁ — מְסָרְגִין אוֹתוֹ מִגּוּפוֹ. מֵיתִיבִי: כְּלֵי עֵץ מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טוּמְאָה? הַמִּטָּה וְהָעֲרִיסָה — מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֵם בְּעוֹר הַדָּג. וְאִי מִטָּה מִסְתָּרֶגֶת עַל גַּבָּהּ, לְמָה לִי שִׁיפַת עוֹר הַדָּג?
אֶלָּא הָא וְהָא מִגּוּפָן. מִטָּה — אַעוֹלֵי וְאַפּוֹקֵי בְּבִזְיָנֵי, דַּרְגֵּשׁ — אַעוֹלֵי וְאַפּוֹקֵי בַּאֲבַקְתָּא.

אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַבִּי: מִטָּה שֶׁנַּקְלִיטֶיהָ יוֹצְאִין, זוֹקְפָהּ וְדַיּוֹ. אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אִידֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.

sections.en: A wooden vessel that was broken into two parts becomes clean, except for a folding table, a dish with compartments for [different kinds of] food, and a householder's footstool. Rabbi Judah says: a double dish and a Babylonian drinking vessel are subject to the same law. When do wooden vessels begin to be susceptible to impurity? A bed and a cot, after they are sanded with fishskin. If the owner determined not to sand them over they are susceptible to impurity. Rabbi Meir says: a bed becomes susceptible to impurity as soon as three rows of meshes have been knitted in it.
sections.he: כָּל כְּלִי עֵץ שֶׁנֶּחֱלַק לִשְׁנַיִם, טָהוֹר, חוּץ מִשֻּׁלְחָן הַכָּפוּל, וְתַמְחוּי הַמִּזְנוֹן, וְהָאֱפִיפוֹרִין שֶׁל בַּעֲלֵי הַבָּיִת. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אַף הַמָּגֵס, וְקוֹד הַבַּבְלִי כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן. כְּלֵי עֵץ, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה. הַמִּטָּה וְהָעֲרִיסָה, מִשֶּׁיְּשׁוּפֵם בְּעוֹר הַדָּג. גָּמַר שֶׁלֹּא לָשׁוּף, טְמֵאָה. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר, הַמִּטָּה, מִשֶּׁיְּסָרֵג בָּהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה בָתִּים:

en:
חָסַם I (Biblical Hebrew; compare preceding wds., [to withhold, prevent, see Ezekiel XXXIX, 11,]
1) to muzzle, especially to prevent the animal from eating while at work (with reference. to Devarim XXV, 4). Bava Metzia 90ᵃ עובר משום בל תַּחְסוֹם he trespasses the law forbidding to muzzle (if he prevents the animal from eating). Ib. חֲסוֹם פרתי muzzle my cow. Ib.ᵇ, and e. חֲסָמָהּ בקול if he prevents her from eating by shouting at her; and from—Transferred (an adaptation of Devarim l. common gender. which is followed by the law concerning leviratical marriage) to tie a woman to a man (Yabam) with whom she cannot live; [Rashi: to shut a woman’s mouth, ignore her objections]. Yevamot 4ᵃ שאין חוֹסְמִין אותה that we do not coërce her (to be the wife of a leper).

—2) to form the rim of basket work or of a leather bag. Kelim XVI, 2; 3; 4.

Nifal - נֶחְסַם to be muzzled, to be prevented from eating while at work. Bava Metzia 89ᵃ לאקושי חוֹסֵם לנֶחְסָם וכ׳ to draw a parallel between the muzzler (human laborer) and the muzzled (laboring brute).

Hithpaël - הִתְחַסֵּם,

Nithpaël - נִתְחַסֵּם to be bent into a rim. Kelim XX, 2.

לָגִין , m. (לגג, see לוֹג, formed like קָצִין)
1) bottle, a vessel smaller than כַּד and larger than כּוֹס. T’bul Yom IV, 4 ל׳ … ומלאהו וכ׳ a lagin which requires sunset to be clean (see טָבַל) and which was filled out of a cask containing tithes (intended for T’rumah); Eruvin 36ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. III, 21ᵇ bottom of page (correct accordingly). Tosefta Oholot V, 10; Oholot V, 4; Chagigah 22ᵇ Manuscript Munich (ed. לוגין); ib. 26ᵃ ל׳ טמאין (read טמא). Pirkei Avot Zar. V, 1 הניח … לְגִינוֹ וכ׳ the gentile put his wine bag on it. Tosefta Terumot VII, 16 ל׳ שהניחו (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) שהניחן, correct accordingly all the suffixes in the sentence); and e.—plural לְגִינִים, לְגִינִין. Tosefta Demai VIII, 22, sq. Kelim XXX, 4 ל׳ גדולים large flasks (of glass). Yerushalmi Chagigah II, end, 78ᶜ. Kelim XVI, 2 בית הל׳ a case of wickerwork for flasks; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 13 בית הליגונין (correct accordingly). Ib. VI, 8 בית הל׳ … של עץ a wooden flask case.—Beitzah 15ᵇ הללו בעלי ל׳ these are people counting their wine by laginin (less rich than the בעלי כדין, but wealthier than the בעלי כוסות).—Yalkut Samuel 161 שבלְגִינוֹת (the water) in the bottles.—
*2) also לְגִינָה f. a garden-bed requiring a lagin of seed. Terumot IX, 5 מאה לגינה Manuscript Munich and Yerushalmi ed. (Bavli and Mishnah ed. לגנה) one hundred beds planted with T’rumah seeds; Tosefta ib. VIII, 4 מאה לגין ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant לגינין; Rabbenu Shimshon to Terumot l. common gender. quotes לוג); [v., however, לִגְנָא].

קָנב , Piël קִינֵּב to strip, trim, make even, clean (vegetable). Kelim XVI, 2 משיחסום וִיקַנֵּב when he has peeled them (the wicker baskets) and trimmed them (pinched off the projecting pricks); ib. 3. Ib. 4 (of leather implements). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VII, 11 (not וינקב); 12. Tosefta Demai IV, 5 לְקַנֵּב, see אִיסְפַּרְגּוֹס. Yerushalmi Pesachim IV, 31ᵃ bottom of page מְקַנֵּב he may clean (vegetable); and e.—Part. pass. מְקוּנָּב. Tosefta Kelim l. common gender. חתוכין ומְקוּנָּבִין cut and cleansed.

comments.en: A kneading-trough: From when is it susceptible to impurity? From the time that its manufacture is completed, and if in the future [one plans] to convert it into a wagon, it is pure. A flask-holder and a cup-holder of palm-fronds, once their rims are rounded off and rough ends are smoothed out from the outside; for even if their rims are not rounded off and their rough ends are not smoothed out from the inside, they are susceptible to impurity because they may remain in that state [and be used]. Small reed baskets and [regular] baskets [are susceptible] once their rims are rounded off and their rough ends smoothed off. Large reed baskets and large partitioned baskets (סּוּגִין) once two rows have been fashioned around their girth, aside from that which is is on the woven part.
comments.he: עריסה מאימתי מקבלת טומאה משתגמר מלאכתה ואם עתיד לעשות לה עגלה טהורה בית הלגינין ובית הכוסות של תמרה שחיסם וקינב מבחוץ שאע"פ שלא קינב מבפנים טמא שכן מקיימין הקנינין הקטנים והקלתות משיחסם ויקניב הקנונין הגדולים והסאין הגדולים משיעשה שני דורין לרוחב שלהן חוץ מזה שעל גבי הארוני נפה וכברה וכף של מאזנים משיעשה דיר לרוחב שלהן חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הקופה משיעשה שתי צבירות לרוחב שלה חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הערק משיעשה בה צבירה אחת חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הסלין של גמלים התירן טהורים קשרן טמאין ומטמאין ומטהרין אפילו עשרה פעמים ביום סלי נצרין שלא קנבן ומשתמש בהן עראי טמאין היה עתיד לחסם ולקלב אע"פ שהוא משתמש בהן עראי ומשליכן טהורים ובלבד שלא יערים ואם הערים הרי אלו טמאין.

sections.en: Wooden baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off. But those that are made of palm-branches [become susceptible to impurity] even though their ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since they are allowed to remain in this condition. A basket [of reed-grass becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its rim is rounded off, its rough ends are smoothed off, and its hanger is finished. A wicker basket flasks or for cups [is susceptible to impurity] even if the rough ends were not smoothed off on the inside, since these are allowed to remain in this condition.
sections.he: הַסַּלִּים שֶׁל עֵץ, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב. וְשֶׁל תְּמָרָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין. כַּלְכָּלָה, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיִגְמֹר אֶת הַתְּלוֹיָה. בֵּית הַלְּגִינִין, וּבֵית הַכּוֹסוֹת, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא קִנֵּב מִבִּפְנִים, טָמֵא, שֶׁכֵּן מְקַיְּמִין:

en: דּוּר II m. (preceding, compare זֵר) rim, wreath. Kelim XVI, 3.—plural דּוּרִים. Ib.

חָסַם I (Biblical Hebrew; compare preceding wds., [to withhold, prevent, see Ezekiel XXXIX, 11,]
1) to muzzle, especially to prevent the animal from eating while at work (with reference. to Devarim XXV, 4). Bava Metzia 90ᵃ עובר משום בל תַּחְסוֹם he trespasses the law forbidding to muzzle (if he prevents the animal from eating). Ib. חֲסוֹם פרתי muzzle my cow. Ib.ᵇ, and e. חֲסָמָהּ בקול if he prevents her from eating by shouting at her; and from—Transferred (an adaptation of Devarim l. common gender. which is followed by the law concerning leviratical marriage) to tie a woman to a man (Yabam) with whom she cannot live; [Rashi: to shut a woman’s mouth, ignore her objections]. Yevamot 4ᵃ שאין חוֹסְמִין אותה that we do not coërce her (to be the wife of a leper).

—2) to form the rim of basket work or of a leather bag. Kelim XVI, 2; 3; 4.

Nifal - נֶחְסַם to be muzzled, to be prevented from eating while at work. Bava Metzia 89ᵃ לאקושי חוֹסֵם לנֶחְסָם וכ׳ to draw a parallel between the muzzler (human laborer) and the muzzled (laboring brute).

Hithpaël - הִתְחַסֵּם,

Nithpaël - נִתְחַסֵּם to be bent into a rim. Kelim XX, 2.

סוֹי m. (נסא = נשא; compare שׂוֹא, Psalms LXXXIX, 10) [load,] large basket. Bava Kamma 20ᵃ ס׳ מקצתו וכ׳ (quot. by R. H. G. to Kelim XVI, 3; ed. מַשּׂוֹי).—plural סוֹאִים, סוֹאִין. Kelim XVI, 3 R. H. G., and Rabbenu Shimshon and l. Variant (ed. סוּגִים); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 1; 13 (quot. by Rabbenu Shimshon l. common gender.; ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) וחסאין, read: וְהַסֹּאִין), see סוּג II.

סוּג II m. (preceding) [partition,] a large chest or basket with partitions for various kinds of provision. Demai V, 6 אפי׳ מאותו הס׳ וכ׳ even if he buys the second time from the same chest and of the same kind (quality). Yerushalmi Bava Kamma II, 3ᵃ ס׳ שנתון וכ׳ a dealer’s chest which stands at the entrance of the shop; and e.—plural סוּגִים, סוּגִין. Kelim XVI, 3 הס׳ הגדולים (Rabbenu Shimshon and l. Variant סוֹאִין; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 3; 13 הסאין, see סוֹי) the large provision chests; Sifra Sh’mini Chaldaic VII, Parah 6 סיגים (correct accordingly). Yerushalmi Shabbat XVII, 16ᵃ bottom of page; and e.—[In later philosophical literature: סוּג class, species.—[Midrash Till. to Psalms CXIX, 119 עושה סוגים, see סִיג I.]

עָרָק, (עֲרָק) m. (see next word)
1) a long and flat vessel made of rush, Maimonides; [oth. opinion sieve; compare אֲרָק and עֲדָק I]. Kelim XVI, 3; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 13.

—2) bandage, compress. Shabbat 54ᵇ Manuscript Oxford, see עֲדָק II.

צְפִירָה II f. (Biblical Hebrew circle, turn; crown; צָפַר, see צְפַר II)
1) circuit. Yerushalmi Eruvin I, end, 19ᵈ (reference. to ויצפר, Judges VII, 3) ולמה הן חוזרין בצ׳ and why were they to go home on a circuitous route?

—2) circle, suite of body-guards. Mekhilta Beshalach, Shir., section (Parashah) 3; Yalkut Shemot 244 מלך … ועליו צ׳ מקיפתו וכ׳ a king that enters a city, and about him is a circle of guards that surrounds him, and his mighty men &c.

—3) a round of twist, border. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 5 סרוד של צ׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) צפורה) a frame with a rim (of plaited ropes &c.), if it has handles, is susceptible of uncleanness. Kelim XVI, 3 משיעשה בו צ׳ אחת as soon as he has woven around it one round (as a rim); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 13 צבירה אחת חוץ מזה וכ׳ (correct accordingly) one round besides the rims of the web itself. Yerushalmi Shabbat VIII, 11ᵇ top באילין קשייא כדי לעשות צ׳ of hard palm-leaves (used for ropes, see אַפְסְקִימָא) as many as are required to make a border; and e.—plural צְפִירוֹת. Kelim l. common gender.; Tosefta l. common gender. צבירות (correct accordingly).

קַלָּת, קַלָּתָה f. (κάλαθος, probably of Semitic origin, see preceding; see Lewy, Sem. Fremdw. p. 109) vase-shaped basket, especially woman’s work-basket. Gittin VIII, 1 זרקו … לתוך קַלָּתָהּ if he throws the letter of divorce into her lap or into her basket. Ib. 78ᵃ כל דבר שהוא כקלתה any receptacle that is designated for her specific use like her basket. Bava Metzia 9ᵇ ק׳ מינח נייחא וכ׳ (if he throws the document into her basket on her head,) her basket is at rest, but she moves under it. Ketubot 72ᵇ top ק׳ שפיר דמי if she goes out with her basket on her head, it is right (she cannot be legally sued for indecent conduct); דת יהודית אפי׳ ק׳ וכ׳ but so far as Jewish custom is concerned, it is improper to go out uncovered even with the basket on the head. Yerushalmi Gittin VIII, beginning 49ᵇ היתה ק׳ של זהב if the basket (into which he threw the letter of divorce) was of gold; and from—plural קַלָּתוֹת. Bikkurim III, 8 העשירים … בק׳ של וכ׳ the rich brought the first-fruits in baskets of silver or of gold. Gittin l. common gender. מוכר ק׳ a dealer in baskets. Kelim XVI, 3; and e.

קָנב , Piël קִינֵּב to strip, trim, make even, clean (vegetable). Kelim XVI, 2 משיחסום וִיקַנֵּב when he has peeled them (the wicker baskets) and trimmed them (pinched off the projecting pricks); ib. 3. Ib. 4 (of leather implements). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VII, 11 (not וינקב); 12. Tosefta Demai IV, 5 לְקַנֵּב, see אִיסְפַּרְגּוֹס. Yerushalmi Pesachim IV, 31ᵃ bottom of page מְקַנֵּב he may clean (vegetable); and e.—Part. pass. מְקוּנָּב. Tosefta Kelim l. common gender. חתוכין ומְקוּנָּבִין cut and cleansed.

קָנוֹן m. (denominative of קָנֶה) a reed basket, contradistinguished to סַל, a common wicker basket. Moʿed Katan III, 7. Beitzah I, 8 (14ᵇ) (missing in Manuscript Munich; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note); Tosefta ib. I, 20; Yerushalmi Ma'asrot IV, 51ᵇ bottom of page; and e.—plural קְנוֹנִים, קְנוֹנִין. Kelim XVI, 3; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 13 (not קני׳).

comments.en: A kneading-trough: From when is it susceptible to impurity? From the time that its manufacture is completed, and if in the future [one plans] to convert it into a wagon, it is pure. A flask-holder and a cup-holder of palm-fronds, once their rims are rounded off and rough ends are smoothed out from the outside; for even if their rims are not rounded off and their rough ends are not smoothed out from the inside, they are susceptible to impurity because they may remain in that state [and be used]. Small reed baskets and [regular] baskets [are susceptible] once their rims are rounded off and their rough ends smoothed off. Large reed baskets and large partitioned baskets (סּוּגִין) once two rows have been fashioned around their girth, aside from that which is is on the woven part.
comments.he: עריסה מאימתי מקבלת טומאה משתגמר מלאכתה ואם עתיד לעשות לה עגלה טהורה בית הלגינין ובית הכוסות של תמרה שחיסם וקינב מבחוץ שאע"פ שלא קינב מבפנים טמא שכן מקיימין הקנינין הקטנים והקלתות משיחסם ויקניב הקנונין הגדולים והסאין הגדולים משיעשה שני דורין לרוחב שלהן חוץ מזה שעל גבי הארוני נפה וכברה וכף של מאזנים משיעשה דיר לרוחב שלהן חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הקופה משיעשה שתי צבירות לרוחב שלה חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הערק משיעשה בה צבירה אחת חוץ מזה שעל גבי האריג. הסלין של גמלים התירן טהורים קשרן טמאין ומטמאין ומטהרין אפילו עשרה פעמים ביום סלי נצרין שלא קנבן ומשתמש בהן עראי טמאין היה עתיד לחסם ולקלב אע"פ שהוא משתמש בהן עראי ומשליכן טהורים ובלבד שלא יערים ואם הערים הרי אלו טמאין.

sections.en: Small reed baskets and baskets [become susceptible to impurity] as soon as their rims are rounded off and their rough ends are smoothed off. Large reed baskets and large hampers, as soon as two rows have been made round their sides. The container of a sifter or a sieve and a cup of the balances, as soon as one circling band has been made round their sides. A willow basket, as soon as two twists have been made around its wide sides. And a rush basket, as soon as one twist has been made round it.
sections.he: הַקְּנוֹנִין הַקְּטַנִּים, וְהַקְּלָתוֹת, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב. הַקְּנוֹנִים הַגְּדוֹלִים, וְהַסּוּגִין הַגְּדוֹלִים, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁנֵי דוּרִים לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶם. יָם נָפָה, וּכְבָרָה, וְכַף שֶׁל מֹאזְנַיִם, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה דוּר אֶחָד לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהֶן. הַקֻּפָּה, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה שְׁתֵּי צְפִירוֹת לָרֹחַב שֶׁלָּהּ. וְהֶעָרָק, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה בוֹ צְפִירָה אֶחָת:

en: *טִרְטֵף (reduplic. of טרף) to cut out edges, to pink. scallop (a leather garment). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VI, 1 משיְטַרְטֵף ed. Vienna (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) and oth. משישטרטף, ed. Zolk. משישוטף) (compare Kelim XVI, 4 משיחסום וכ׳ &c.).

חָסַם I (Biblical Hebrew; compare preceding wds., [to withhold, prevent, see Ezekiel XXXIX, 11,]
1) to muzzle, especially to prevent the animal from eating while at work (with reference. to Devarim XXV, 4). Bava Metzia 90ᵃ עובר משום בל תַּחְסוֹם he trespasses the law forbidding to muzzle (if he prevents the animal from eating). Ib. חֲסוֹם פרתי muzzle my cow. Ib.ᵇ, and e. חֲסָמָהּ בקול if he prevents her from eating by shouting at her; and from—Transferred (an adaptation of Devarim l. common gender. which is followed by the law concerning leviratical marriage) to tie a woman to a man (Yabam) with whom she cannot live; [Rashi: to shut a woman’s mouth, ignore her objections]. Yevamot 4ᵃ שאין חוֹסְמִין אותה that we do not coërce her (to be the wife of a leper).

—2) to form the rim of basket work or of a leather bag. Kelim XVI, 2; 3; 4.

Nifal - נֶחְסַם to be muzzled, to be prevented from eating while at work. Bava Metzia 89ᵃ לאקושי חוֹסֵם לנֶחְסָם וכ׳ to draw a parallel between the muzzler (human laborer) and the muzzled (laboring brute).

Hithpaël - הִתְחַסֵּם,

Nithpaël - נִתְחַסֵּם to be bent into a rim. Kelim XX, 2.

טִרְטֵט (טרט = רטרט, compare גִּעֲגֵעַ; see טָרוּט
2) to plait straps, to strap. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VI, 1 משיְטַרְטֵט ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant משיְרַטֵּט) until the leather for the strap-mattress is plaited; (compare Kelim XVI, 4).

סְקוֹרְטְיָא, סְקוֹרְטְיָה f. (scortea, subaudi vestis; see אִיסְקוֹרְטְיָא) leather coat;also leather apron. Kelim XVI, 4 (Maimonides leather table-cover, see צִיצָה). Ib. XXVI, 5 (6) עור ס׳ the skin intended for a scortea. Oholot VIII, 1 ס׳ a leather bed-sheet. Tosefta Shabbat V (VI), 14. Nedarim 55ᵇ, [read as:] Yerushalmi ib. VII, end, 40ᶜ; Tosefta ib. IV, 3Nedarim 55ᵇ, [read as:] Yerushalmi ib. VII, end, 40ᶜ; Tosefta ib. IV, 3 איסק׳; and e. [Ned. l. common gender. מאי איסק׳ כיתונא דצלא scortea is a leather coat.]

צִיצָה f. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding wds.)
1) flower, knob on the top of the central stem of the palm branch (Lulab). Yerushalmi Sukkah III, beginning 53ᶜ יבשה צִיצָתוֹ (ed. Krot., and Asheri to Sukkah III, beginning צִיצִיתוֹ; Asheri quotes a Variant יבשו הוצין) if the top of the branch is withered.

—2) fringes. Gittin 56ᵃ שהיתה ציצתו נגררת וכ׳ the fringes of his cloak were dragged along on cushions. Moʿed Katan III, 4 תכלת לציצתו Yerushalmi ed. (Mishnah and Bavli ed. 19ᵃ לציציתו; Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) quotes לציצתו) the blue thread for his show-fringes.—Kelim XVI, 4 סקורטיא … ויעשה את צִיצָתָהּ (Arukh ציציתיה, read: צִיצוֹתֶיהָ) a leather apron is considered finished, when … he attaches its fringes (cords); [Maim.: a leather table cloth …, when he puts on a bright center piece].—plural צִיצוֹת, see supra.

קִיחָה f. (לָקַה)
1) = לְקִיחָה, taking, acquiring. Yevamot 97ᵃ (reference. to Vayikra XX, 11-14) בכולן נאמר שכיבה וכאן נאמר ק׳ וכ׳ with reference to all of them the word ‘sleeping’ is used, but here (see 14) ‘taking’ is used, to intimate that the law punishes the marriage only (and not the sexual connection out of wedlock). Ib. הכי נמי הנך ק׳ הוא וכ׳ do you really say with reference to these (see 17) that the law forbids only marriage? (Answer) ליקוחין … הראוי לק׳ ק׳ וכ׳ the verb laḳaḥ is used as a general term: where a regular marriage might have taken place (under other circumstances), the text prohibits marriage; where only sexual connection can be meant, the verb laḳaḥ has the meaning of shakhab. Kiddushin 2ᵃ, and e. גמר ק׳ ק׳ וכ׳ we learn the mode of acquiring (לקח in Devarim XXII, 13) from the acquisition of the field of Ephron (Breishit XXIII, 13 קח); Chullin 82ᵃ; and from—plural קִיחוֹת. Yoma 3ᵇ בק׳ דעלמא וכ׳ in general cases where the text uses קח, …, but here (Shemot XXX, 23) it says expressly קח לך (take unto thee, at thy own expense).

—2) [handle,] leather thong, loop. — plural as ab. Kelim XVI, 4 התורמל … קִיחוֹתָיו (Arukh קיה׳, Variant קיח׳) the shepherd’s bag is susceptible of uncleanness, when one has made the rim, trimmed it, and attached the thongs with which to tie it up. Ib. קִיחוֹתֶיהָ the thongs of the leather spread.

קָטָבוֹלְיָא, קָטָבוֹלְיָה, קָטָבְלְיָא, (קָטָבְלָא) f. (corresp. to a word καταβολία; compare κατάβλημα) a (leather) curtain, spread, cover. Kelim XVI, 4 ק׳ the hide spread over the bed-frame. Tosefta Shabbat III (IV), 17 קיטבליא חדשה (Variant קטבליא, טבלה) a new leather spread; Yerushalmi ib. VI, 8ᵃ קטיבלייא; Tosefta Terumot X, 11 קיטבילא ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant קטבוליא); Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 28ᵃ bottom of page קטיב׳. Kelim XXVI, 5 (6) עור קטבוליא Mishnah ed. (Talmud ed. קטבולין) the hide which is used as a spread. Bava Metzia 90ᵇ פרס לה קיטבליא ע"ג דישה (Manuscript Munich קטביל׳; Manuscript Florence קרטבליא) if he spread a leather cover over the grain to be threshed (preventing the ox from eating); and e.—plural (from קָטַבְלִי καταβολή) קָטָבְלָאוֹת, קָטַבְלָיוֹת. Shekalim III, 4 מחפה בק׳ (Manuscript Munich קיטבל׳) he covered (last year’s contributions) with leather spreads. Yerushalmi ib. III, end, 47ᶜ שמט את הקטבליו׳ (ed. Krot. הקטבליי׳; Bavli ed. קטבליאות; Manuscript Munich קיטבלאות) when the covers are removed; Tosefta ib. II, 4 שמנו ק׳ (correct accordingly).

קָנב , Piël קִינֵּב to strip, trim, make even, clean (vegetable). Kelim XVI, 2 משיחסום וִיקַנֵּב when he has peeled them (the wicker baskets) and trimmed them (pinched off the projecting pricks); ib. 3. Ib. 4 (of leather implements). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VII, 11 (not וינקב); 12. Tosefta Demai IV, 5 לְקַנֵּב, see אִיסְפַּרְגּוֹס. Yerushalmi Pesachim IV, 31ᵃ bottom of page מְקַנֵּב he may clean (vegetable); and e.—Part. pass. מְקוּנָּב. Tosefta Kelim l. common gender. חתוכין ומְקוּנָּבִין cut and cleansed.

comments.en:
Leather vessels: From what point are they susceptible to impurity (Kel. 16:4)? A sandal, once the straps are attached. A shoe, once it is placed on the [shoemaker's] mold, and if he intends to varnish it, [it is not susceptible] until he varnishes it; and if he intends to make designs [on it], [it is not susceptible] until he makes designs. A leather coat, before it is scalloped. A leather hide [used as a bedspread], before it is moistened. The leather [cover] of a crib that he intends to make into an infant's naval string (tibur), it is pure until he makes it into an infant's naval string. Rabbi Yehuda says a leather cushion [becomes susceptible if] not less than five [handbreadths remain open], and a leather mattress [becomes susceptible if] not less than three [handbreadths remain open] (contra. Kel. 16:4 (five each)).
Bone vessels: From what point are they susceptible to impurity? From the time that their manufacture is completed. [If] they lack their outer covering, they are impure. A shofar is pure, [but] if he cut a horn into pieces [to use as a vessel], it is impure. A horn that he uses and then discards it is pure, [but if] he thinks about [using it as a vessel], it is susceptible to impurity from that point onward. A mat for dates that he intends to throw away once the dates are eaten is pure, [but if] he thinks about carrying it in and out of his house, or [in and out] of his field, it is impure.
comments.he: כלי עור מאימתי מקבלין טומאה הסנדל משיקמע והמנעל משיגוב מעל האימום ואם עתיד לכרכב עד שיכרכב ולשרטט עד שישרטט איסקורטיא משישטרטף וקורטבליא משירטט עור העריסה שהוא עתיד לעשות לו טיבור טהור עד שיעשה לו טיבור רבי יהודה אומר בכר אין פחות מחמשה ובכסת אין פחות משלשה. כלי עצם מאימתי מקבלין טומאה משתגמר מלאכתה מחוסרים כסויין טמאין שופר טהור חתכו לקרן טמא הקרן שהוא משתמש בה ומשליכה טהורה חשב עליה מקבלת טומאה מכאן ולהבא חותל של תמרה שהוא עתיד לאכול התמרה ולזורקו טהור חשב להכניס ולהוציא בו מן הבית ומן השדה טמא.

sections.en: When do leather vessels become susceptible to impurity?A leather pouch, as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough ends trimmed and its straps sewn on. Rabbi Judah says: so soon as its ears have been sewn on. A leather apron [becomes susceptible to impurity] as soon as its hem has been stitched, its rough end trimmed and its strings sewn on. Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its loops have been sewn on. A leather bed cover [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed. Rabbi Judah says: as soon as its straps have been sewn on. A leather cushion or mattress [becomes susceptible] as soon as its hem has been stitched and its rough ends trimmed. Rabbi Judah says: as it has been sew up and less than five handbreadths remained open.
sections.he: כְּלֵי עוֹר, מֵאֵימָתַי מְקַבְּלִין טֻמְאָה. הַתּוּרְמֵל, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה קִיחוֹתָיו. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת אָזְנָיו. סְקֹרְטְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב וְיַעֲשֶׂה אֶת צִיצָתָהּ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת טַבְּעוֹתֶיהָ. קָטָבוֹלְיָא, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיַּעֲשֶׂה אֶת קִיחוֹתֶיהָ. הַכַּר וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁל עוֹר, מִשֶּׁיַּחְסֹם וִיקַנֵּב. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, מִשֶּׁיִּתְפְּרֵם וִישַׁיֵּר בָּהֶם פָּחוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה טְפָחִים:

en: חֲסִינָה f. (see חִסְנָא) [storage,] a wicker work used for purposes of storage. Kelim XVI, 5.

חוֹתָל common gender. (חתל Biblical Hebrew to tie around, swaddle) wrapper of reed-matting in which dates are packed, bale. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VI, 4 ח׳ של וכ׳ a mat for dates which is intended to be thrown away when the dates are eaten. Kelim XVI, 5 ח׳ שהוא וכ׳ a bale which you can add to or take from (without cutting it open) &c. Yerushalmi Shabbat I, end, 4ᵇ ח׳ שהוא מלא וכ׳ a bale filled with fruit stones. 'Uktzin II, 2, see חוֹתָם.—[Yerushalmi Ketubot VIII, 32ᵇ top מלא חותלה אסי וכ׳, read ר׳ אסי וכ׳, חותל …]—plural חוֹתָלוֹת. Shabbat 146ᵃ

סִגְנִיּוֹת f. plural (see סְגֵי I, compare מוּרְבִּית) [made of twigs, leaves,] loosely woven mats used for covering up fruit. Kelim XVI, 5 ס׳ של עלין (Rabbenu Shimshon סוּגְ׳) mats made of leaves; ס׳ של נצר of wicker.—[סיגניות, Yalkut Shemot 232, see סִיגְנוֹן.]

פְּטַלְיָא, פְּטַלְיָה, פְּטִילְ׳ f. (פטל, see preceding) wickerwork, especially a sort of bale for packing dates, figs &c. Tosefta Shabbat XII (XIII), 15 פ׳ של גרוגרות מקרע וכ׳ you may cut open a bale of figs (on the Sabbath) and eat; Yerushalmi ib. XV, beginning 15ᵃ פטילייא. Kelim XVI, 5 פְּטַלְיָה ed. Dehr. (ed. פּטילייה). Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni I, 52ᵈ פטולייא של תמרים a bale of dates, contradistinguished from חוֹתָל; and e.—plural פְּטַלְיָאוֹת. Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni I, 10 פ׳ ודרוסות של תמרה ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (ed. omit פ׳) dates packed in bales, and date pomaces.

קָרַע (Biblical Hebrew) to tear, split; especially to rend the garment in mourning. Kelim XVI, 5 עד שיִקְרְעֶנּוּ (Mishnah ed. שיַקְרִיעֶנּוּ Hifil) until he tears the bale open. Moʿed Katan 22ᵇ על כל … אינו קוֹרֵעַ אלא עליון for all dead (except parents) … one must rend only the upper garment. Ib. האשה קוֹרַעַת וכ׳ a woman (mourning for her parents) rends the lower garment and puts it back in its place, and then rends the upper garment. Sanhedrin 60ᵃ אחד השומע … חייב לִקְרוֹעַ both he that hears a blasphemy directly, and he that hears it from one that heard it (and reports as witness before court) must rend his garment; and see from—Part. pass. קָרוּעַ; plural קְרוּעִים, קְרוּעִין. Moʿed Katan 26ᵇ היוצא בבגד ק׳ וכ׳ he that marches before a corpse with a garment rent (for a previous case) robs (deceives) the dead and the living. Ib.ᵃ (reference. to II Kings II, 12) ק׳ ועומדים לשנים remaining always rent in two; ib. 22ᵇ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 4); Sanhedrin l. common gender.; and from

Piël - קֵרֵעַ
1) same. Moʿed Katan 26ᵇ ואין מְקָרְעִין בפניו you must not rend your garment in his (the sick man’s) presence. Ib. מקרעין לקטן וכ׳ we rend a minor’s garment in order to make him feel sad; ib. 14ᵇ. Rosh Hashanah 16ᵇ ארבעה … מקרעין גזר וכ׳ four things cause an evil decree passed on man to be torn (cancelled), they are: charity, prayer &c.; and from

—2) (compare גָּרַע) to scrape, to mark the outlines of letters by abrasion. Gittin 19ᵇ עדים … מקרעין להם וכ׳ for witnesses that know not how to sign their names, grooves are made on blank paper, and they fill the grooves out with ink; ib. 9ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. II, 44ᵇ top ומְקָרֵעַ; [Tosaf. to Gittin 9ᵇ: you cut the names out on blank paper and put it on the document, and the witnesses fill the cuts out]. Tosefta Shabbat XI (XII), 8, contradistinguished from רשם; and e.

Nifal - נִקְרַע to be torn; to be cut open, be operated upon by a section. Yevamot VIII, 6, and e. טומטום שנ׳, see טוּמְטוּם. Bekhoroth 42ᵇ שמא יִקָּרֵעַ וכ׳ he may have an operation performed, and be found a eunuch; Tosefta Yevamot XI, 1; Yevamot 83ᵇ. Bava Batra 168ᵇ נ׳ פסול נִתְקָרֵעַ כשר if a document is found torn, it is invalid; if it appears torn by accident, it is valid as evidence; ib. נ׳ קֶרַע של בית דין נתק׳ וכ׳ miḳrʿa refers to the rent as made in court for cancellation, nithḳareʿa refers to a rent different from the manner customary in court; Yerushalmi Gittin II, 44ᵇ; and e.

Nithpaël - נִתְקָרֵעַ to become torn, see supra.

comments.en: In practice the halakha follows the lenient position, because these bags have no importance and are thrown out after the food they contain is finished. Therefore, one may open them in whatever way enables easy removal of their contents, and he may use them until the food inside is used up.
comments.he: למעשה, הלכה כדברי המקילים, שכן אין חשיבות לשקיות אלו, שזורקים אותן לאחר שהמאכל הנמצא בהן נגמר, ולכן מותר לעשות בהן פתח נוח להוצאת תכולתן, ולהשתמש בהן עד סיום המאכל שבתוכן.

sections.en: A basket [for figs] is susceptible to uncleanness but a basket for wheat is clean. Small baskets made of leaves are clean, but those made of branches are susceptible to uncleanness. The palm wrapping [in which dates are left] and into which they can be easily put  and from which they can easily be taken out is susceptible to uncleanness, but if this cannot be done without tearing it or undoing it, it is clean.
sections.he: פָּטִילְיָה, טְמֵאָה. וַחֲסִינָה, טְהוֹרָה. סִגְנִיּוֹת שֶׁל עָלִין, טְהוֹרוֹת. שֶׁל נְצָרִין, טְמֵאוֹת. חוֹתָל שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן לְתוֹכוֹ וְנוֹטֵל מִתּוֹכוֹ, טָמֵא. וְאִם אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל עַד שֶׁיִּקְרָעֶנּוּ אוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּתִּירֶנּוּ, טָהוֹר:

en: פִּשְׁתָּן f. same. Kilayim IX, 1. Yerushalmi ib. 31ᵈ מה פ׳ כברייתה, see preceding Ib. פ׳ של ים (Maimonides to Kilayim IX, 1 פשתים) seaflax (tangle). Kelim XVI, 6 עושי פ׳ workers in flax. Sifra Thazr., Negaim, Parah 5, Chaldaic XIII אונים של פ׳, see אוּנִין. Ib. Chaldaic XV, אניצי פ׳, see אָנִיץ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 32; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 16 פשתני זה כשפִּשְׁתָּנוֹ קשה וכ׳ when his flax is hard, the flax-worker does not beat it too much וכשפשתנו יפה וכ׳ but when his flax is good, the more he beats it, the better it grows; so the Lord tries not the wicked &c.; and from

קְסִיָּיה f. (קסי = כָּסָה II) [cover, protection,]
1) a sort of glove for laborers. Kelim XVI, 6 (ed. Dehr. קְסִיָּה).

—2) ק׳ של שלחנות table cloth, a sheet spread over the set table to protect it from flies &c. Makhshirin V, 8 קסיה ed. Dehr. (ed. קסיא); [Ar.: vessels, compare קִסְוָה,—which, however, does not suit the context].

sections.en: The leather glove of winnowers, travelers, or flax workers is susceptible to uncleanness. But the one for dyers or blacksmiths is clean. Rabbi Yose says: the same law applies to the glove of grist dealers. This is the general rule: that which is made for holding anything is susceptible to uncleanness, but that which only affords protection against perspiration is clean.
sections.he: קְסָיָה שֶׁל זוֹרֵי גְרָנוֹת, שֶׁל הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים, שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂי פִשְׁתָּן, טְמֵאָה. אֲבָל שֶׁל צַבָּעִין וְשֶׁל נַפָּחִין, טְהוֹרָה. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת כַּיּוֹצֵא בָהֶן. זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְקַבָּלָה, טָמֵא. מִפְּנֵי הַזֵּעָה, טָהוֹר:

en: *גְּנוֹגְנִית, גְּנוֹגֶנֶת f. (גנן, compare גִּנּוּן) a sort of parasol made of osier and used by field laborers. Kelim XVI, 7 גנוגנת העני Arukh (Mishnah גְּנוֹגְנוֹת plural, Talmud ed. גנוגנית, Maimonides comment. ed. Derenbourg גְּנוֹנֶת). [Ar. and Rabbenu Shimshon: the poor man’s bag.]

*סוּת, סֶוֶת f. (Biblical Hebrew; סוה , see מַסְוֶה) dress, cloak. Kelim XVI, 7 עושה ס׳ ed. Dehr. (oth. ed. סְוָתוֹת or סוּתוֹת plural), see אִמּוּם. [Var. in Mishnah ed. סיאגוס, probably meant for סָאגוֹס = סָגוֹס, as a gloss to our word; Rabbenu Shimshon to Kelim l. common gender. שיאגות, Variant סבאות; Hai G. סאיכות, Variant סְיָאוֹת.]

אִמּוּם, אִימּוּם m. (= אמאום, denominative of אֵם) model, form, shoe-maker’s last, &c. Kelim XXVI, 4; XXIII, 1.—Ib. XVI, 7 הא׳ של גודלי וכ׳ the block of the cap-makers; של עושי וכ׳ of dressmakers. Shabbat 141ᵇ Manuscript Munich (ed. אימוס, correct accordingly); and from
אַלְיָית, אַלְיָת f. (אלי II) female wailer. Kelim XVI, 7 רביעית של א׳ the wailer’s musical instrument. Ib. XV, 6.—Chaldaic אָלְיְתָא see as well

אַנְלוֹגִין m. (ἀναλογεῖον) reading desk, pulpit. Kelim XVI, 7 Arukh אנלגין (Variant in Rabbenu Shimshon אנליגין, ed. אנגלין; correct accordingly). Yerushalmi Megillah III, 73ᵈ bottom of page אנג׳, אינג׳ (correct accordingly). Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma II, 3 או לולגין פרוס׳ וכ׳ ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant אלו לגין, ed. אולו לוגין read אנאלוגין; used as fem.) a reading desk spread out is clean, folded together is unclean (susceptible of levitical uncleanness).

גָּדַל II (see preceding; compare גדש) [to heap up, round;] to plait, dress the hair. Kelim XVI, 7 גּוֹדְלֵי מצנפות capweavers (on a model head, see אִמּוּם). Ib. XV, 3 וגוֹדְלוֹת and dress their hair. Shabbat X, 6 הגּוֹדֶלֶת she who plaits her hair (on the Sabbath). Ib. 94ᵇ bottom of page גודלת משום אורגת plaiting the hair (is forbidden on the Sabbath) as an act of weaving; ib. 95ᵃ (another opinion) ג׳ … משום בונה as an act of building. Yerushalmi ib. VII, 10ᵈ הגודל כלי צורה he who forms raised figures on a vessel. Moʿed Katan 11ᵃ ג׳ תנור to build a stove.

דְּבוֹרָה f. (Biblical Hebrew דְּבֹרָה; דבר to lead, join)
1) [swarm,] bee. Yalkut Devarim 795 (play on הדברים, Devarim I, 1) מה הד׳ הזו בניה מתנהגין וכ׳ as the bee is followed by the young, so are the Israelites led by the righteous &c.; (Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 1 כדְּבוֹרִים היו וכ׳ like bees my children were guided &c.). Ib. מה הד׳ הזו וכ׳ as the bee whose honey &c.; and from—plural דְּבוֹרִים. Kelim XVI, 7 מדף של ד׳ the vessel used for smoking the bees out. Bekhoroth 7ᵇ דבש ד׳ bee-honey. Devarim Rabbah l. common gender., see supra.

—2) proper noun of a female person Deborah, the heroine and prophetess. Megillah 14ᵃ; and from—שִׁירַת ד׳ the song of Deborah (Judges V). Yerushalmi Megillah III, 74ᵇ bottom of page; Masechet Sof’rim XII, 10; and e.
זַמָּר m. (זָמַר I) musician, singer. Kelim XVI, 7 מרכוף של ז׳, see מַרְכּוֹף. Yalkut Eicha 1001.
חֲסוֹם, (חוֹסָם) m. (חָסַם I; Biblical Hebrew muzzle. Kelim XVI, 7 (ed. Dehr. חִיסּוּם; Mishnah ed. חסים, incorr.). Tosefta Shabbat IV (V), 5 חוסם; Shabbat 53ᵃ

טָפוּס m. (טָפַף, see דָּפוּס) frame, mould. Kelim XVI, 7 ט׳ של תפלה the block on which the case of the phylacteries is shaped. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, 28ᵈ top ט׳ של פעור a cast of the idol P’or; (Sifré Bamidbar 131 דפיס; Sanhedrin 106ᵃ יראתה). Yerushalmi Shabbat IV, 8ᵇ bottom of page ט׳ של דדים, see דָּפוּס. Demai V, 4 (ed. Yerushalmi טִיפּוּס). Yerushalmi ib. 24ᵈ top נחתום עושה ט׳ אחד if the baker makes only one form of loaves. Ib. (once) טופוס אחד (correct accordingly); and e.—Pt. טְפוּסִין. Demai V, 3 (Arukh דפ׳). Yerushalmi ib. l. common gender. נחתום … כמה ט׳ if the baker makes several forms of loaves. Ib. שני טפסין (correct accordingly).—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VI, 4 טִיפּוּסִים של פעור, see supra.

מְנָפָה f. (נוּף)
1) fan. Kelim XVI, 7 (Arukh מנפא). Yevamot 63ᵃ במ׳ תתנופפי Arukh, see נוּף Chaldaic—V. מְנִיפָא.—
*2) (see מַפָּה) flag.—plural מְנָפוֹת. Mekhilta Beshalach, section (Parashah) 2 מגפות (correct accordingly); see, however, סִיגְנוֹן.
מַדָּף m. (נָדַף) a vessel used for smoking bees out, see דְּבוֹרָה. Kelim XVI, 7.

מַכְבֵּשׁ m. (כָּבַשׁ) clothes-press; screw, vise. Tosefta Shabbat XVI (XVII), 5 מ׳ של בעלי … כלים (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) מים for כלים, correct accordingly) a domestic clothes-press which has been unscrewed to take out clothes. Shabbat XX, 5 מ׳ … מתירין וכ׳ you may unscrew a domestic clothes-press but not screw it (on the Sabbath). Ib. (מ׳)של כובסין the washers’ clothes-press. Kelim XVI, 7 מ׳ של חרש the carpenter’s vise (for straightening wood), see מְכַוֵּון; Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 8 מכביש של נגר. Ib. 15 מ׳ של שכף וכ׳ the leather worker’s press on which he stretches the hides. Yerushalmi Shabbat XX, end, 17ᵈ; and e.

מַלְקוֹט m. (לָקַט) bag. Kelim XVI, 7 המ׳ של בקר the bag for receiving the excrements of working cattle; [Tosaf. Yom. Tob and l. attests a version מַקְלוֹט]. [Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia III, 14, see מְלַקֵּט II.]
מַקְלוֹט m. (קָלַט) bag for collecting the excrements of working cattle Yerushalmi Bava Kamma II, beginning 2ᵈ. Kelim XVI, 7, see מַלְקוֹט.

מַרְכּוֹף, (מַרְכּוֹב) m. (compare אַרְכּוֹף) markof, name of a musical instrument made stationary. Kelim XV, 6 המ׳ טהור the m. (used in the Temple) is not susceptible of uncleanness. Ib. XVI, 7 מ׳ של זמר the m. used for the accompaniment of songs; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia V, 10.
קִמְרוֹן m. (קָמַר) arched lid. Kelim XVI, 7. Ib. XVIII, 2.

קַמְטְרָא, קוּמְ׳ m. (κάμπτρα = κάψα) box, chest (for clothes, books &c.). Kelim XVI, 7, contradistinguished to קופסא. Oholot IX, 15. Berakhot 25ᵇ sq. גלימא אק׳ a cloak spread over a box (containing sacred books); and e.—plural (Chaldaic) קוּמְטְרַיָּא, קוּמְטְרִין, קַמְטְרֵי. Targum Sheni (to Esther) Kings X, 22 (Regia קֻמְ׳). Targum Ezekiel XXVII, 24 (Regia קוּמְטַרְוָן; ed. Lag. קַמְטַרְוָון).—Megillah 26ᵇ ק׳ דספרי book chests.
קַפְצָה f. (an adapt. of capsa, as if from קָפַץ) chest, box. Kelim XVI, 7 ed. Dehr. (ed. קופסא). Yerushalmi Niddah II, beginning 49ᵈ ק׳ של זכוכית a glass box.—plural קַפְצָיוֹת. Ib.

קוּלָב I m. (compare next word) [grappler,] a stand with steps, and with nails and hooks for the exhibition of goods in front of a shop; rack. Shabbat 60ᵃ top; Yerushalmi ib. VI, 8ᵇ; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia III, 13. Sifra Sh’mini, Chaldaic VII, Parah 6 (quot. in Maimonides to Kelim XVI, 7 הקֶלֶב); Yalkut Vayikra 538.

קוּפְסָא f. (capsa) box for books &c. Targum Yonatan Devarim XXXI, 26.—Kelim XVI, 7 כסוי של ק׳ (ed. Dehr. קפצה) the lid of a box. Menachot 41ᵃ כלי ק׳ (Maimonides to Kelim l. common gender. ed. Dehr. קופצא) garments in a box; Yalkut Devarim 933 קוּפְסִין (plural). Midrash Till. to Psalms XII ק׳ מלאה וכ׳ a box full of gold Denars; ib. קוטמא כולה וכ׳ (ed. Bub. קיט׳, correct accordingly) the whole box is of gold on the outside; Yalkut ib. 656.

רְבִיעִית f. h.
1) same. Kelim XVI, 7
(see Maimonides and l.).—2) fem. of רְבִיעִי
see as well—3) square block. Tamid III, 5, see רָבִיעַ.

comments.he: מכל כלי עץ או בגד וכולי: מ"ם של "מכל" לא באה כפי הדקדוק. שהיה לו לכתוב "כל כלי עץ וכולי" כדין פרט המבאר את הכלל. וזה כלל בחוקי הלשון שכל מקום שבאו כמה שמות ביחוס אחד והם כולם מחלק הצדדי במשפט צריך שיבוא סימן היחוס עם כל אחד ואחד – "מהעוף ומן הבהמה מכל רמש האדמה" (בראשית ו, כ), "ומארצות קבצם ממזרח וממערב מצפון ומים" (תהלים קז, ג). (וכמו שכתבנו באילת השחר (כלל רח)). ואם כן היה צריך לומר פה "מכל כלי עץ או מבגד או מעור". ועל כרחך שהמ"ם של "מכל" אינו נצרך לסימן היחוס (שלא בא פה ביחוס שממנו), רק המ"ם "מכל" מורה הקצתיית, שלא כל כלי עץ מטמאים רק מקצת מהם. וזה סותר עם מלת "כל" שבא לכלול שכולם מטמאים. ובזה יש פה ריבה ומיעט. ולא נוכל לדעת מהו הכללות המטמא ומהו המקצת היוצא מן הכללות שאינו מטמא. ובזה צריכים אנו לעיין על יתר הפרטים שבאו פה. כי כבר בארנו שמדרך הלשון שנושאים המקובצים במשפט אחד יהיה להם איזה השתוות וזה ענין ההיקש (כמ"ש באילת השחר כלל קס). ובין הפרטים חשב שק והוא מבואר בענינו וצורתו. ונדמה הסתום אל המפורש; שהדומה לשק הוא בכלל הריבוי והבלתי דומה הוא בכלל המיעוט. והשק מצאנו בו שני ענינים: (א) שהוא משמש את האדם להתכסות בו ואת משמשי האדם – כי יניח בו כליו וחפציו. וזה הגדר הראשון שחשב בספרא [משנה ד'] (מובא בתוספות סוכה דף ה, מנחות דף צו, ובפירוש הר"ש פרק טז דכלים מ"ז. ועיין תוספות בבא בתרא (דף סו), עירובין (דף לא) מה שכתבו על הספרא הלז). ור"ל הסולם משמש רק את האדם והקולב (פירש הרמב"ם דפוס שנקרא בערבי קלב. והראב"ד שהשיג (פ"ד מהלכות כלים) על הרמב"ם ופירש קלב סולם והביא ראיה מהתורת כהנים על כרחך היה גרסתו "ומוציא אני את הסולם והקלב שהם משמשים את האדם". אבל בתוספתא הכי איתא "העשוי לשמש את האדם כגון הסולם, ואת הכלים כגון הקלב"). והנחותה – כלי שמניחים תחת הכלים. והמנורה שהם משמשים רק למשמשי האדם. לכן הם טהורים. ולר' יוסי במשנה דכלים (משנה כלים פ"טז מ"ז) יש גדר שלפעמים גם משמשים משמשי האדם טמאים גם משמש את הכלים בשעת מלאכה ושלא בשעת מלאכה. (ב) הגדר הב' שהשק מטלטל מלא וריקן כמו שכתוב "ויהי הם מריקים שקיהם". וזה מה שחשב [במשנה ה'] (מובא בר"ש פרק ט"ו דכלים מ"א ופירושו מבואר במשנה שם). והשדה והתיבה וכל אינך מנה ר' מאיר במשנה שם לטהרה. ואמר דיתר הכלים אף מקבלים מ"ם סאה טמאים. ודרדור עגלה וקסתות המלכים וכולי מנה ר' יהודה במשנה שם לטומאה אף שמקבלים מ"ם סאה כי דרך לתת שם רק קצת ולטלטלם במלואם. ועל זה אמר ר' מאיר [במשנה ו] שכל מקום שחשב בטהרה טהור והשאר טמא, ור' יהודה שחשב את הטמאים לבד אמר שהשאר טהור. ואין ביניהם אלא עריבת בעל הבית שלר' מאיר טמאה אחר שלא חשבוה עם הטהורים ולר' יהודה טהורה כיון שלא חשבוה בין הטמאים. ודברי ר' נחמיה מובנים שאלו הכלים, אף על פי שאין מטלטלים מלאים, מטלטלים אם נשתייר בהם פחות ממ"ם סאה. ודברי ר' נחמיה מובאים בתוספתא דכלים (ב"מ פ"ה).

sections.en: The dung bag of a bull and its muzzle, a bee shelf, and a fan are clean. The cover of a small box is susceptible to uncleanness; The cover of a clothes chest is clean. The cover of a box, the cover of a basket, a carpenter's vice, a cushion under a box or its arched cover, a reading-desk for a book, a bolt-socket, a lock-socket, a mezuzah case, a lyre case, a violin case, the block of the turban-makers, a wooden musical toy horse, the clappers of a wailing woman, a poor man's parasol, bed posts, a tefillin mould, and the mould of string makers all these are clean. This is the general rule which Rabbi Yose stated: all objects that serve as a protection to objects that a man uses, both when the latter are in use and when they are not in use, are susceptible to uncleanness; but those that serve them as a protection only when the latter are in use are clean.
sections.he: הַמַּלְקוֹט שֶׁל בָּקָר, וְהֶחָסִים שֶׁלּוֹ, וְהַמַּדָּף שֶׁל דְּבוֹרִים, וְהַמְּנָפָה, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין. כְּסוּי שֶׁל קֻפְסָא, טָמֵא. כְּסוּי קַמְטְרָא, טָהוֹר. כְּסוּי תֵּבָה, כְּסוּי טֶנִי, וְהַמַּכְבֵּשׁ שֶׁל חָרָשׁ, וְהַכֶּסֶת שֶׁתַּחַת הַתֵּבָה, וְהַקִּמְרוֹן שֶׁלָּהּ, וְאַנְגְּלִין שֶׁל סֵפֶר, בֵּית הַנֶּגֶר, בֵּית הַמַּנְעוּל, וּבֵית הַמְּזוּזָה, וְתִיק נְבָלִין, וְתִיק כִּנּוֹרֶת, וְהָאֵמוּם שֶׁל גּוֹדְלֵי מִצְנָפוֹת, וְהַמַּרְכּוֹף שֶׁל זַמָּר, וּרְבִיעִית שֶׁל אַלָּיִת, וּגְנוֹגְנִית הֶעָנִי, וְסָמוֹכוֹת הַמִּטָּה, וּטְפוּס שֶׁל תְּפִלָּה, וְאֵמוּם שֶׁל עוֹשֵׂה סוּתוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִים. זֶה הַכְּלָל, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, כָּל מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי מְשַׁמְּשָׁיו שֶׁל אָדָם בִּשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה וְשֶׁלֹּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָמֵא. וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִשְׁעַת מְלָאכָה, טָהוֹר:

en:
אַלָּה f. (Biblical Hebrew Joshua XXIV, 26; see אַלָּתָא) [pointed, prominent]
1) lance, fork. Kelim XVI, 8 חפוי הא׳, see חִפּוּי. Pesachim 57ᵃ אוי לי מֵאַלָּתָן woe to me (I am afraid) of their fork (weapon). Shabbat VI, 3 (63ᵃ) ed. (Manuscript אלא); Yerushalmi ibid. 8ᵇ (explained דייקרן).

—2) sign-pole, used in the barn as a mark. Ib.; Yerushalmi Ma'asrot I, 49ᵃ bottom of page; Tosefta Terumot III, 11 משתיעקר הא׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) משיתעשר, correct accordingly) as soon as the sign-pole (fork) is removed (indicating that the grain is ready for use and priestly gifts).

חִפּוּי, חִי׳ m. (preceding)
1) covering, wrapping. Kelim XVI, 8 (חעשוי) לח׳ whatever is intended for wrapping, opposed תיק, casing. Ib. XXVI, 6. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra IV, 11; and e.—plural חִפּוּיִם, חִי׳. Ib. XVI, 8 חִפּוּיֵ האלה וכ׳ the wrapping of a lance &c.

—2) upholstered seat. Ib. XXII, 4 a bridal chair שנטל חִפּוּיוֹ whose seat is missing; (Eduy. I, 11 חִפּוּיָו, Manuscript Munich דפניו, Mishnah Nap. חופיו, see Rabad and l.). Kelim l. common gender. 6 שנטל חִפּוּיוֹ האמצעי whose middle cushion (of the three forming the seat) is wanting.—plural as ab. Ib. 5 שלא היו חִפּוּיָו יוצאין (ed. Dehr. חִפּוּיָיו) whose seats were not movable (see Rabad to Eduy. l. common gender.); and from—[Tosefta Shabbat IV (V), 7 כל חיפוי ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta), read with ed.: נוֹי.]

מִסְפֶּרֶת, מִסְפּוֹרֶת f. (preceding) shearing knife, clipping tool. Kelim XVI, 8, see preceding Moʿed Katan 17ᵇ, and e., see preceding Kelim XIII, 1 (Maimonides מספו׳, ed. Dehr. מספרת). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia III, 4 מ׳ של פרקים shears consisting of separable blades; Shabbat 48ᵇ; 58ᵇ מספו׳. Tosefta Beitzah III, 19, see סָפַר; and e.

מַסְפָּרַיִים, מַסְפָּרַיִם m. du. (preceding) shears, scissors. Kelim XVI, 8 תיק מספרת ומ׳ the sheath of a shearing knife or of scissors. Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan III, 82ᵃ top במ׳ with scissors, contradistinguished to סכין and מספרת; Bavli Moʿed Katan 17ᵇ; and e.—[Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia IV, 5 מספרים ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta), read מַסְמְרִים.]

סִימְפּוֹנְיָא, סִימְפּוֹנְיָה, סִימְפּוֹנְיָיא, סִמְ׳ f. (Daniel III, 5 סוּמְפּנְיָה; 10 סִיפּנְיָה, Ketubot סוּפּ׳; 15 סומפניה; see preceding, and compare סבכא, שבכא Daniel ll. cc.) [air-passages, compare meanings of σύριγξ,] simponia (Greek adapt. συμφωνία), a wind instrument, double flute. Kelim XI, 6 ס׳ אם יש בה בית קיבול כנפים if the simp. has a receptacle for the wings (i.e. a bagpipe); Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia I, 7. Kelim XVI, 8 סמפ׳ Mishnah ed. and ed. Dehr. (Talmud ed. סִפּוֹנְיָא).—[Midrash Till. to Psalms XII, beginning עסוקים בהדי סימפוניא ed. Bub. (oth. ed. עוסקים בההיא סמפניא; Variant in Mss. עוסקים הוסמפניא, הוסתיא &c., see ed. Bub. note; Yalkut Psalms 656 עסוקים בהדיה ספסוני׳, a corruption in a spurious passage; perh. to be read: בהוֹרוֹסְקוֹפְיָא (ὡροσκοπία) engaged in horoscopy.]
פָּגוֹז m. (פגז, compare פגש) battering projectile.—plural פָּגוֹזוֹת בית הפ׳; catapult. Kelim XVI, 8 ed. Dehr. (ed. פגושות).
פָּגוֹזָא Chaldaic same. —plural פְּגוֹזִין. Targum Ezekiel XXVI, 9 פְּגוֹזוֹהִי (Maimonides to Kelim XVI, 8 quotes פְּגוֹשׁוֹהִי; ed. Dehr. פגוז׳).

תֵּיק m. (θήκη) casing, sheath. Kelim XVI, 8 העשוי לת׳ whatever is intended for a casing, contradistinguished to חִפּוּי. Shabbat XVI, 1 ת׳ הספר a book chest; ת׳ התפלין a box or bag in which the T’fillin are kept; and from

תרונתק , read: תְּרוּנַק, or תְּרוּנְקֵס m. (θρίναξ) trident, fork, used as a tool in writing, probably for levelling the paper (compare Lat. charta dentata). Kelim XVI, 8 תיק מכתב ות׳ תיק וכ׳ the case for the stylus and the trident, the case of &c.—[The corruption of our word arose from a dittography of the next following word תק or תיק,—which gave rise to the etymology תרין־תק.—Hai Gaon explains our word with המנק.]

sections.en: The sheath of a sword, a knife or a dagger, the case for scissors, or shears or a razor, the case of make-up and the make-up box, the stylus case, the compass case, the tablet case, the case for a board, a quiver and a javelin case all these are susceptible to uncleanness. The case for a double flute is susceptible to uncleanness if the instrument is put in from above, but if it is put in from the side it is clean. A case for flutes Rabbi Judah says it is clean because these are put in from the side. The covering of a club, a bow or a spear is clean. This is the general rule: that which serves as a case is susceptible to uncleanness, but that which is merely a covering is clean.
sections.he: תִּיק הַסַּיִף וְהַסַּכִּין וְהַפִּגְיוֹן, תִּיק מִסְפֶּרֶת וּמִסְפָּרַיִם וְהַתַּעַר, תִּיק מִכְחוֹל, וּבֵית הַכּוֹחַל, תִּיק מַכְתֵּב, וּתְרוּנְתֵּק, תִּיק טַבְלָא וּסְקֹרְטְיָא, בֵּית הַחִצִּים, בֵּית הַפָּגוֹשׁוֹת, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְמֵאִים. תִּיק סִמְפּוֹנְיָא, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא נוֹתֵן מִלְמַעְלָה, טָמֵא. מִצִּדּוֹ, טָהוֹר. תִּיק חֲלִילִין, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מְטַהֵר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא נוֹתְנוֹ מִצִּדּוֹ. חִפּוּי הָאַלָּה, הַקֶּשֶׁת, וְהָרֹמַח, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ טְהוֹרִין. זֶה הַכְּלָל, הֶעָשׂוּי לְתִיק, טָמֵא. לְחִפּוּי, טָהוֹר:
